front: Petit à petit, l'oiseau fait son nid.
pronunciation: [puh-tee tah puh-TEE, lwah-zoh feh sohn NEE]
back: Little by little, the bird builds its nest.
context: Slow, steady effort pays off. Compare 'Rome wasn't built in a day'.

front: Rome ne s'est pas faite en un jour.
pronunciation: [ROM nuh seh pah fet ahn nan ZHOOR]
back: Rome wasn't built in a day.
context: Note 'faite': Rome (a city) is feminine here.

front: L'habit ne fait pas le moine.
pronunciation: [lah-bee nuh feh pah luh MWAN]
back: Don't judge a book by its cover.
context: Literally 'the habit doesn't make the monk'.

front: Il n'y a pas de fumée sans feu.
pronunciation: [eel nyah pah duh fü-may sahn FUH]
back: There's no smoke without fire.
context: Same as in English.

front: Qui se ressemble s'assemble.
pronunciation: [kee suh ruh-sahm-bluh sah-SAHM-bluh]
back: Birds of a feather flock together.
context: Literally 'those who resemble each other gather'.

front: Tout vient à point à qui sait attendre.
pronunciation: [too vyan tah PWAN ah kee seh tah-TAHN-druh]
back: Good things come to those who wait.
context: 'À point' = at the right moment (also 'medium' for steak).

front: Qui ne risque rien n'a rien.
pronunciation: [kee nuh reesk RYAN nah RYAN]
back: Nothing ventured, nothing gained.
context: A favorite of entrepreneurs.

front: Loin des yeux, loin du cœur.
pronunciation: [lwan day ZYUH, lwan dü KUHR]
back: Out of sight, out of mind.
context: Literally 'far from the eyes, far from the heart'.

front: On ne fait pas d'omelette sans casser des œufs.
pronunciation: [ohn nuh feh pah dum-LET sahn kah-say day ZUH]
back: You can't make an omelet without breaking eggs.
context: Note: 'des œufs' is pronounced 'day-zuh' (silent f in the plural).

front: Chat échaudé craint l'eau froide.
pronunciation: [shah ay-shoh-DAY kran loh FRWAHD]
back: Once bitten, twice shy.
context: Literally 'a scalded cat fears even cold water'.

front: La nuit porte conseil.
pronunciation: [lah NWEE port kohn-SAY]
back: Sleep on it.
context: Literally 'the night brings advice'.

front: Les murs ont des oreilles.
pronunciation: [lay MÜR ohn day zoh-RAY]
back: Walls have ears.
context: A warning to speak discreetly.

front: C'est en forgeant qu'on devient forgeron.
pronunciation: [seh tahn for-ZHAHN kohn duh-vyan for-zhuh-ROHN]
back: Practice makes perfect.
context: Literally 'it's by forging that one becomes a blacksmith'.

front: Quand le chat n'est pas là, les souris dansent.
pronunciation: [kahn luh SHAH neh pah LAH, lay soo-REE DAHNS]
back: When the cat's away, the mice will play.
context: Used about employees when the boss is on holiday.

front: Qui sème le vent récolte la tempête.
pronunciation: [kee sem luh VAHN ray-kolt lah tahm-PET]
back: Sow the wind, reap the whirlwind.
context: From the Bible (Hosea).

front: L'appétit vient en mangeant.
pronunciation: [lah-pay-TEE vyan tahn mahn-ZHAHN]
back: The more you have, the more you want.
context: From Rabelais (16th c.). Also used to encourage someone to just start.

front: À cheval donné, on ne regarde pas les dents.
pronunciation: [ah shuh-val doh-NAY, ohn nuh ruh-gard pah lay DAHN]
back: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth.
context: Same image as in English.

front: Tant va la cruche à l'eau qu'à la fin elle se casse.
pronunciation: [tahn vah lah KRÜSH ah LOH kah lah FAN el suh KAS]
back: If you keep pushing your luck, it will run out.
context: Literally 'the jug goes to the water so often that in the end it breaks'.

front: Une hirondelle ne fait pas le printemps.
pronunciation: [ün nee-rohn-DEL nuh feh pah luh pran-TAHN]
back: One swallow doesn't make a summer.
context: French says 'spring', not summer. 'Hirondelle' has a silent h, so 'une-n-hirondelle'.

front: Les chiens aboient, la caravane passe.
pronunciation: [lay SHYAN ah-BWAH, lah kah-rah-VAN PAS]
back: Let them talk; we carry on regardless.
context: An Arabic proverb popular with French politicians facing critics.

front: Qui trop embrasse mal étreint.
pronunciation: [kee troh pahm-BRAS mah lay-TRAN]
back: Don't bite off more than you can chew.
context: Literally 'who embraces too much holds poorly'.

front: Il ne faut jamais dire : Fontaine, je ne boirai pas de ton eau.
pronunciation: [eel nuh foh zhah-meh DEER : fohn-TEN, zhuh nuh bwah-reh pah duh tohn NOH]
back: Never say never.
context: Literally 'never say: fountain, I will not drink your water'.

front: On n'apprend pas à un vieux singe à faire des grimaces.
pronunciation: [ohn nah-prahn pah ah an vyuh SANZH ah fehr day gree-MAS]
back: You can't teach an old hand any new tricks.
context: Literally 'you don't teach an old monkey to pull faces': an experienced person already knows every trick.

front: Charbonnier est maître chez soi.
pronunciation: [shar-boh-NYAY eh MEH-truh shay SWAH]
back: A man's home is his castle.
context: Literally 'the charcoal maker is master in his own home'.

front: Aide-toi, le ciel t'aidera.
pronunciation: [ed-TWAH, luh syel teh-duh-RAH]
back: God helps those who help themselves.
context: From La Fontaine's fable 'Le Chartier embourbé'.

front: Rien ne sert de courir ; il faut partir à point.
pronunciation: [ryan nuh sehr duh koo-REER ; eel foh par-teer ah PWAN]
back: Slow and steady wins the race.
context: First line of La Fontaine's 'Le Lièvre et la Tortue' (1668).

front: La raison du plus fort est toujours la meilleure.
pronunciation: [lah reh-zohn dü plü FOR eh too-zhoor lah meh-YUHR]
back: Might makes right.
context: La Fontaine, 'Le Loup et l'Agneau': ironic, not an endorsement!

front: Tout flatteur vit aux dépens de celui qui l'écoute.
pronunciation: [too flah-TUHR vee oh day-PAHN duh suh-lwee kee lay-KOOT]
back: Every flatterer lives at the expense of those who listen.
context: The moral of 'Le Corbeau et le Renard', the most famous French fable.

front: Chose promise, chose due.
pronunciation: [shohz proh-MEEZ, shohz DÜ]
back: A promise is a promise.
context: Literally 'a thing promised is a thing owed'.

front: Deux précautions valent mieux qu'une.
pronunciation: [duh pray-koh-SYOHN val myuh KÜN]
back: Better safe than sorry.
context: Literally 'two precautions are better than one'.

front: En avril, ne te découvre pas d'un fil ; en mai, fais ce qu'il te plaît.
pronunciation: [ahn nah-VREEL, nuh tuh day-koo-vruh pah dan FEEL ; ahn MEH, feh suh keel tuh PLEH]
back: Don't shed a thread in April; in May, do as you please.
context: Weather wisdom: don't put away your warm clothes too early.

front: Il ne faut pas mettre la charrue avant les bœufs.
pronunciation: [eel nuh foh pah meh-truh lah shah-RÜ ah-vahn lay BUH]
back: Don't put the cart before the horse.
context: French uses a plough and oxen. 'Bœufs' plural: the f is silent.

front: Il faut appeler un chat un chat.
pronunciation: [eel foh tah-puh-lay an SHAH an SHAH]
back: You have to call a spade a spade.
context: Boileau popularized it: 'J'appelle un chat un chat'.

front: Faute de grives, on mange des merles.
pronunciation: [foht duh GREEV, ohn mahnzh day MEHRL]
back: Beggars can't be choosers.
context: Literally 'for lack of thrushes, we eat blackbirds'.

front: La critique est aisée, mais l'art est difficile.
pronunciation: [lah kree-TEEK eh teh-ZAY, meh LAR eh dee-fee-SEEL]
back: It's easy to criticize, harder to do.
context: From the 18th-century playwright Destouches.

front: Le mieux est l'ennemi du bien.
pronunciation: [luh MYUH eh len-mee dü BYAN]
back: Perfect is the enemy of good.
context: Attributed to Voltaire.

front: Il ne faut pas jeter le bébé avec l'eau du bain.
pronunciation: [eel nuh foh pah zhuh-tay luh bay-BAY ah-vek loh dü BAN]
back: Don't throw the baby out with the bathwater.
context: Same image as in English.

front: Une de perdue, dix de retrouvées.
pronunciation: [ün duh pehr-DÜ, dee duh ruh-troo-VAY]
back: There are plenty more fish in the sea.
context: Said to console someone after a breakup.

front: Les bons comptes font les bons amis.
pronunciation: [lay bohn KOHNT fohn lay bohn zah-MEE]
back: Short reckonings make long friends.
context: Settle money matters clearly to keep friendships healthy.

front: Il faut battre le fer pendant qu'il est chaud.
pronunciation: [eel foh bah-truh luh FEHR pahn-dahn keel eh SHOH]
back: Strike while the iron is hot.
context: Same blacksmith image as in English.

front: Les cordonniers sont toujours les plus mal chaussés.
pronunciation: [lay kor-doh-NYAY sohn too-zhoor lay plü mal shoh-SAY]
back: The shoemaker's children go barefoot.
context: Literally 'shoemakers are always the worst shod': experts neglect their own needs.

front: Pierre qui roule n'amasse pas mousse.
pronunciation: [pyehr kee ROOL nah-mas pah MOOS]
back: A rolling stone gathers no moss.
context: In French, it's usually a criticism of instability.

front: Tel est pris qui croyait prendre.
pronunciation: [tel eh PREE kee krwah-yeh PRAHN-druh]
back: The biter is bitten.
context: From La Fontaine: the trickster gets tricked.

front: Il ne faut pas réveiller le chat qui dort.
pronunciation: [eel nuh foh pah ray-veh-yay luh SHAH kee DOR]
back: Let sleeping dogs lie.
context: French uses a sleeping cat instead of a dog.

front: Ça, c'est une autre paire de manches.
pronunciation: [SAH, seh tün NOH-truh pehr duh MAHNSH]
back: That's a whole different ball game.
context: Literally 'another pair of sleeves': from detachable sleeves in the Middle Ages.
